newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse head sees 25 new listed firms in '97.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse head sees 25 new listed firms in '97.

text.p: The president of the Warsaw Stock Exchange expects about 25 firms and the 15 National Investment Funds (NFI) to join the 83 firms already listed next year, the Parkiet financial daily reported on Wednesday.
Wieslaw Rozlucki said the funds, which control more than 500 firms under Poland's mass privatisation scheme, are expected to enter the bourse in 1997's first half.
"I'm counting on the 15 National Investment Funds and about 25 new firms. I hope that at least one or two of them will be large privatised firms," Parkiet quoted Rozlucki as saying.
Several large privatisations are slated for next year, including those of copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz SA and Bank Handlowy SA.

Securities Commission head Jacek Socha told the paper that he expected the number of entities approved for public trade to rise to 150 or 170 from the current 101, including about 30 firms to be listed on the nascent over-the-counter market.
